Nov 23 (Reuters) - CrowdStrike will acquire Zscaler in a $43.9 billion all-stock deal, the biggest cybersecurity acquisition on record, uniting two major players in the field as AI advances fuel increasingly sophisticated cyber threats.
Shares of Zscaler rose more than 18% in premarket trading to $231.40 but were still trading well below the implied offer price of $260.41 per share. CrowdStrike fell more than 8%.

CrowdStrike shareholders will own about 84% of the combined company after the transaction closes, which is expected in the second half of 2027.
George Kurtz, CrowdStrike's CEO, will lead the combined company, while Zscaler chief executive Jay Chaudhry will stay on to run the Zscaler business and join CrowdStrike's board.
The companies will continue to operate separately until closing. The agreement carries a $1.4 billion breakup fee payable by Zscaler if it walks away under certain circumstances, including to accept a rival offer.

The combined company is expected to start with more than $10 billion in annual recurring revenue, including roughly $3.9 billion from Zscaler.
